title: Dryrun retro template, hourly cadence, and signal scoring (2026-04 draft)
body:
Purpose
This is a working template for a pre-launch dryrun. The file captures an hour-by-hour cadence (H-2 -> H+6), a lightweight signal-scoring rubric to gate rollout decisions, operator cue cards for common failure modes, and retro prompts to convert dryrun learnings into actionable improvements. Use this in conjunction with the release checklist and the runbook (see linked artifacts).

Scope and objectives
- Validate run-of-show and comms flow under constrained incident scenarios.
- Exercise telemetry anchors and alert thresholds; ensure owner escalation works.
- Check model routing fallbacks and quick rollback path.
- Produce a prioritized retro with concrete owners and timelines.

Pre-dryrun prep checklist (owners in parens)
- Confirm dry data set and synthetic probes loaded to staging (SRE).
- Confirm canary traffic steering configuration in Traffic Router (Infra).
- Verify preserved KV cache warmup recipe and prefix caching flags (Serving Runtime).
- Provision ephemeral burn buckets for load testing (Infra).
- Slack channel: #release-dryrun-<date> created and pinned messages (PM).
- Paging list validated (oncall pager + escalation matrix) (SRE lead).
- Smoke test scripts and post-hook alarms available in GH PR #4567 (Dev).

Hour-by-hour cadence (annotated)
H-2: final preflight (30–45m)
- Confirm oncall roster and handoff notes posted.
- Quick walkthrough of rollback plan and readme link.
- Run synthetic health probes against model endpoints (p50/p95 latency sanity).
- Activate sampling telemetry (trace-level enable) for the dryrun window.

H-1: staging full-circuit run (60m)
- Run smoke flow: request -> routing -> model -> response validation.
- Exercise KV cache warm path and verify cache hit ratio > 65% for prefix workload.
- Run failover: intentionally disable primary model node, validate fallback model spin-up.
- Capture logs: set retention to 72h for artifacts.

H: light canary (30m)
- Start with 1% traffic; monitor core signals and canary signal score.
- Operator notes: keep throttles at baseline; do not change routing unless signal score crosses red.

H+0.5: ramp check (30m)
- Increase to 5% if all green.
- Validate cost telemetry tags are appearing (per-route token counting).

H+1: mid-ramp (60m)
- Increase to 20% assuming green.
- Create telemetry snapshot and attach to retro doc.

H+2: steady state observation (60m)
- Hold at target (e.g., 50%) for stress window if needed.
- Run synthetic perturbations: latency spike (add 100–200ms), token-rate burst, model quality regression (inject failing prompts).

H+3..H+6: fallout scenarios and rollback drills
- Trigger a partial rollback from 50% -> 5% and observe rollback recovery path.
- Test regional failover (simulate AZ outage).
- Validate canary-to-prod promotion checklist and final notes.

Signal scoring rubric (use integer score 0–3; 0=good, 3=critical)
- p99 latency (inference): 0 if <150ms; 1 if 150–300ms; 2 if 300–600ms; 3 if >600ms.
- Error rate (5xx/model failures): 0 if <0.05%; 1 if 0.05–0.25%; 2 if 0.25–1%; 3 if >1%.
- Model quality drift (eval prompt set): 0 if >98% pass; 1 if 95–98%; 2 if 90–95%; 3 if <90%.
- Token throughput consumption (cost spike): 0 if within expected ±10%; 1 if +10–25%; 2 if +25–50%; 3 if >50%.
- Observability gaps (missing metrics/traces): 0 if full coverage; 1 if minor gaps; 2 if important gaps; 3 if critical missing signals (cannot make decision).
- Combined decision: sum scores, then map: 0–3 = green (proceed), 4–6 = amber (pause/mitigate), 7+ = red (rollback/abort).

Operator cue cards (short actionable scripts)
- High p99 latency (p99>300ms):
  1) Check runtime node CPU/GPU utilization and model queue depth.
  2) Flip traffic to lower-latency variant (Routing -> model-variant v1-q8) using the quickflip play.
  3) If no improvement within 3m, scale extra serving replicas (autoscale override +10%).
  4) Alert oncall and set status to amber; capture timeline.

- Increased error rate (5xx >0.25% sustained 2m):
  1) Pull latest logs for model handler exceptions (search: "handler: exception").
  2) Disable problematic model shard; route to fallback.
  3) If >1% persist, initiate rollback to previous stable model version.

- Quality regression detected (eval set fail rate crosses threshold):
  1) Pause ramping; switch to holdback variant for 100% of canary traffic.
  2) Notify product and research; collect failing prompt examples.
  3) Open a bug epic and assign triage owner.

Comms snippets (copy-paste for Slack/Email)
- Slack canary-green: "DRYRUN UPDATE: Canary 1% -> green. p99=128ms, errors=0.02%, quality pass=99.1%. Proceeding to 5% in 10m. —@oncall"
- Slack canary-amber: "DRYRUN ALERT: Canary at 5% showing elevated p99=420ms and error=0.4%. Pausing ramp, investigating. Oncall @sre taking lead. Details: <brief link to telemetry snapshot>."
- Exec note (email): "Quick note: Dryrun found a latency regression in the new runtime kernel under burst traffic. We exercised rollback and observed normal service recovery. Action owner: Miguel T (kernel tuning) to follow up by 2026-06-20."

Post-dryrun retro template (fill during/after session)
- Timestamped incidents observed (list, include H+ markers).
- Who was involved (roles + Slack handles).
- What worked well (3 bullets).
- What failed / surprised us (3 bullets).
- Root cause hypotheses and evidence (attach logs/traces).
- Action items (owner, due date, severity tag).
- Follow-up required with product/security/infra? (yes/no + notes).

Suggested immediate action item examples
- Improve p99 telemetry dashboard to include model queue latency (owner: SRE, due: 2026-06-17).
- Add synthetic prompt set for quality regression detection to CI (owner: Research, due: 2026-06-25).
- Harden fallback routing scripts and test in CI (owner: Platform, due: 2026-06-22).

Draft release notes skeleton (to be copied into release-notes doc)
- Summary: Small-batch rollout to new inference kernel with improved memory efficiency. Dryrun date: 2026-06-10.
- What changed: Updated runtime kernels, canary routing rules, and observability sampling.
- Known issues: Under high-burst synthetic traffic p99 increased; temporary mitigation: fallback to previous kernel variant.
- Rollout plan: Gradual ramp with defined canary gates; rollback path documented in the runbook.
- Contacts: Claire Nguyen (release lead), Miguel Torres (runtime), Aisha Patel (SRE).

Notes and open questions
- Do we want a separate, lower-noise channel for exec updates (short summary + link)?
- Should synthetic perturbations be part of every dryrun or only once per major kernel change? Recommendation: keep for kernel/quantization changes.
- Are we comfortable with the current combined decision threshold? We'll test it on two more dryruns before locking.

Quick reference links (copy into runbook)
- Runbook (confluence): CONFLUENCE-ROLLUP-4521
- Dryrun test scripts: GH PR #4567
- Escalation matrix: JIRA: ROLL-789

-- end of template --

(Notes: this is intentionally succinct and action-oriented. Fill in timestamps and attach telemetry snapshots during the dryrun. Keep notes informal — this doc is for the team to iterate rapidly.)
